abstract: By annealing a cold rolled 30Mn-13Al-1.3C-5Cr steel at $1 0 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ we successfully developed a novel lightweight steel having the tensile strength of 1250 MPa and total elongation of 41.4 % at the measured ultralow density of 6.36 g⋅cm<sup>-3</sup>. Such an unprecedented strength-ductility-density synergy results from the new designed austeniteferrite duplex microstructures, where the granular α ferrite grains can restrain the austenite grain growth, δ ferrite bands capture and deflect the propagating cracks, and high contents of Mn/Al/C in recrystallized austenite result in the extensive precipitation of κ-carbide nanoparticles for strengthening Due to the high demand for weight saving and energy conservation, the lightweight Fe-Mn-Al-C steels have received an increasing attention in many industries [1–3] due to their excellent combination of specific strength and ductility [2,4,5]. Among all the relevant researches, Moon et al. [6] set a record on their developed 29.05Mn-12.01Al-1.48C-5.13Cr (weight percentage unless mentioned elsewhere) austenitic steel, which has the specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) of 169.9 MPa⋅g<sup>-1</sup>⋅cm<sup>3</sup> and total elongation (TE) of 43.8 % at the density of 6.34 g⋅cm<sup>-3</sup>. To our knowledge, this is almost the lowest density achieved in a highly deformable Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic steel with the SUTS up to 170 MPa⋅g<sup>-1</sup>⋅cm<sup>3</sup>. A further improvement on specific strength via lowering density is clearly more challenging, because lower density requires higher contents of Al/C added, which often lead to the brittle inter granular κ-carbides formed at grain boundaries, severely deteriorating ductility [7,8]. A promising pathway of further improving the specific strength-ductility synergy at such a low density is in lack but strongly desired. Ferrite is more effective on reducing density than austenite because body centered cubic (BCC) structure has lower atomic density than face centered cubic (FCC) [1,9]. Meanwhile, the presence of ferrite phase results in an inhibition on the growth of austenite grains and many austenite/ferrite interfaces, which may improve yield strength (YS) and the strain hardening capacity during deformation [10]. Therefore, it is expected that the austenite-ferrite duplex structure may have greater potential of improving the strength-ductility-density synergy than the mere austenitic one. However, the reported austenite-ferrite duplex steels all have the density higher than 6.50 g⋅cm<sup>-3</sup> [11–20], to our knowledge, and it has been instinctively believed that cracks may be easily initiated at the austenite/ferrite interfaces and then propagate along them, thus dramatically deteriorating ductility [21]. For an example, Sohn et al. [13] reported that the increase of ferrite fraction from 13.2 % to 32.3 % in 12Mn-5.5Al-0.7C duplex steel (with the den sity of 7.20 g⋅cm<sup>-3</sup>) led to the increases of the SUTS from 139.3 to 196.5 MPa⋅g<sup>-1</sup>⋅cm<sup>3</sup> but the significant decrease of TE from 45.9 % to 8.2 %. This, however, may also suggest that it shall be possible to improve the SUTS-TE combination by optimizing the presence of ferrite. Therefore, we consider to redesign the previous ultralow density steel (29.05Mn-12.01Al-1.48C-5.13Cr [6]) for the austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure, through which SUTS can be further enhanced while low density and large ductility both remain.
section_headings: Unprecedented combination of specific tensile strength and ductility achieved in a novel duplex low-density steel
